# OpenVMM runtime: fourth release candidate

This release updates OpenVMM to 0.4.0 and fixes the KVM guest CPU identity.
The guest now sees the CPUID hypervisor-present flag even when Hyper-V
enlightenments are disabled, allowing Linux to skip bare-metal CPU initialization
and uncore discovery paths that probe unavailable MSRs.

- Apply the CPUID fix as a patch to a commit-pinned OpenVMM checkout,
  prepared automatically by `mise run openvmm-prepare`. Core source files are
  fetched during preparation rather than copied into this repository.
- Preserve the existing FUSE decoder hardening, shared-directory permission
  policy, and per-device virtio-net MTU support.
- Include OpenVMM 0.4.0 fixes for serial-console boot delays when host CPU time
  is constrained and stale state-unit dependencies after device removal.
- Add CPUID regression tests and offline tests of checkout preparation, patch
  updates, commit verification, and protection of local edits.
- Ship the GPL-3.0 license and third-party notices with source links, including
  the upstream OpenVMM revision and local patch. Normalize Debian release asset
  names and organize build, networking, storage, and test documentation.

Publication requires the release workflow's Linux and Windows native checks,
RustSec audit, Linux KVM integration tests, packaging, and checksum verification.
The reported AMD-host MSR messages still require verification on the affected
machine; the unit tests establish the CPUID policy, not that host-specific result.
Actual Windows WHP guest execution remains unverified.
